# Implementation slices and dependencies

Current product owner: [LevitateOS/factory](https://github.com/LevitateOS/factory),
extracted on 2026-11-03. Continue this queue in the Factory checkout. Go owners
formerly under `internal/` now live under `pkg/`. Earlier completed rows retain
their original SodaOS/Fountain evidence; extraction does not rerun or extend that
qualification. Forge's Go, UI and native consumer cutovers are committed in its
own repository. Initial extraction snapshots remain in Git history; recovery
patches and inactive archived coordinator tests are retired from the working
tree. Connected and installed parity still require their stated journeys.
See the [current repository guide](../../../README.md).

This is the executable backlog for the [plan](ideal-filetree-plan.md), now being
implemented Linux first with Tauri. Slice completion requires the stated result,
not merely file movement. M = mechanical extraction, C = named behavior correction, V = real
verification. Native/installed evidence remains a separate gate from source checks.

## Sequential implementation order

The table is the canonical dependency graph and work queue. T00–T14 below are
scope families; implement the named slices here, not a whole family at once.
Every prerequisite is a **completed slice**, including its stated verification.
The row order is a valid topological order and the default execution order;
independent rows may proceed only when an earlier row is genuinely blocked.
No dashed completion dependencies or implicit producer handoffs are used.

Existing progress is retained: the shared feed, thirteen Storybook states and Linux
Tauri component rendering already work. They do not complete T04-UI, the native
runtime or connected collaboration. **T00-PG, T01-REGISTRY and T01-LEDGER are
complete**. **T01-RECORDS, T01-EFFECTS and T01-RUNTIME are also complete**.
**T00-DIFF, T02-INTAKE, T02-GRAPH and T02-RUN-OBSERVATIONS are complete**.
**T02-PREP-OBSERVATIONS is complete**. It was split from T02-RUNS before
implementation; completed command/ledger work stays retained in that partial
consumer slice. **T02-PREP-CONSUMERS is complete**: the canonical record, store
and preparation command callers moved together. **T02-RUNS is complete**, including
launch/profile construction and native admission refusal. **T02-ID-STORAGE is complete**, split from T02-IDENTITIES before implementation.
**T02-ID-RESOLUTION is complete**, split before the identity consumer cutover.
**T02-ID-COMPOSITION is complete**: appliance Factory construction atomically
binds its configured Fountain source before coordinator construction.
**T02-ID-REQUEST-ACTORS is complete**, split from the remaining identity cutover
before request composition. **T02-ID-RUNTIME is complete**, split before appliance
launch-actor conversion. **T02-IDENTITIES is complete**: control/store/API Project joins, signed events,
service readiness, Factory API repository authorization/settings and Fountain
feed/project-work catalogue wiring now use scoped mappings. Shared settings resolve
their native Project binding before Factory reads/writes. Request places now use
canonical ownership, repository selection and scoped drafts. Workspace setup and
watch consumers now separate native custody from canonical Factory scopes. Feed
subscriptions, human authorship, product-change ownership and activity/repair
attribution are canonical. Native intake proofs/receipts now translate through
the adopted Fountain host. Creation recovery now maps repository/creator scopes
at its native read boundary. Graph reads/authorization, operations, receipt
projection and feedback now translate their native scopes. Completion enumeration
and ref capture resolve native scope while local material stays canonical.
Publication, correction payloads and adopted receipts now translate native scope.
Review and thread-resolution adapters now translate observations, packets and
receipt/readback scope as well. Delivery-judgment discussion resolves native
access scope and returns canonical participants with exact native bodies/digests.
Check and merge adapters now resolve their native
scope and return canonical approval/merger attribution. Feed repository keys now
use decimal strings across API/host/shared UI consumers; native identity discovery
also passes through the Fountain frontend proxy. The identity consumer cutover
and current scoped-client recovery are qualified below. **T02-ENGINE is complete**
at the Linux source/integration boundary. **T03-FEED is complete**: its shared
application service supplies transport-independent
feed windows/projections and canonical subscription CAS. **T03-POSTS is complete**:
the shared service owns durable post routing/draft/effect and background recovery.
**T03-AUTHORING is complete**: funded post authoring now uses the shared service
and resumes its recorded planning attempt across restart. **T03-CAPTURE is complete**:
the shared service now owns capture-first Issue Maker orchestration and uncertain
refinement recovery. **T03-REQUEST-READS is complete**: owner-private overviews
and saved-review reads use shared application logic with an explicit runtime
setup port. **T03-REQUEST-WRITES is complete**: request/department saves and
private catalogue reads use the shared service with current repository admission.
**T03-PLANNING is complete**: admitted draft-planning and recorded-plan generation
commands use shared orchestration, including recovery with a fresh coordinator.
**T03-EXPLORATION is complete**: exploration, planning status/walkthrough review
and generation reads now use the shared service and durable judgment records.
**T03-SCOPE-HISTORY is complete**: owner-private structural comparisons,
generation lineage and mapped-work authority use the shared service too.
**T03-POST-VIEWS is complete**: admitted post/record/reply views and product-review
handoff now use shared visibility, private-data and action-capability logic.
**T03-POST-COMMANDS is complete**: submission/retry use explicit provider-capture
ports and recover saved source identities even after parent changes.
**T03-CONTRIBUTIONS is complete**: the shared continuation now owns bounded
contribution claims, independent Choice calls and cancellation-safe settlement.
**T03-CATALOGUE is complete**: registered repositories can be paged through a
shared service and admitted Fountain HTTP without native Project inventory.
**T03-CATALOGUE-UI is complete**: the global feed uses that catalogue instead of
Spaces, with scoped page validation and visible incomplete-list recovery.
**T03-VERIFICATION is complete**: private verification-limit reads and grants use
the shared request service, with current admission and a transactional repository

**T03-ISSUE-CONTEXT is complete**: admitted context capture and saved routing

**T03-POLICY is complete**: repository policy assembly/admission use the shared

**T03-ACTIVITY is complete**: confirmed activity reads and display-setting saves

**T03-JOURNEY is complete**: the recorded issue-work journey and all its evidence

**T03-ISSUE is complete**: the full issue-work response now uses shared assembly,

**T03-WORK-READS is complete**: admitted assignment and priority-comparison panels

**T03-STATUS is complete**: repository status uses explicit runtime/admission

**T03-SPONSORSHIP is complete**: sponsorship uses current visibility/custody

**T03-ACCESS is complete**: settings powers, required actions and private usage

**T03-INTERVENTIONS is complete**: repository and run commands now use shared

**T03-RUN-STATUS is complete**: run status/context/delivery projections use

**T03-REPAIR-FUNDING is complete**: repair allowance/history and grant commands

**T03-OUTPUT is complete**: read-only output uses shared canonical attachments,

**T03-ACCEPTANCE is complete**: exact-input preview/admission/withdrawal use

**T03-POST-EFFECTS is complete**: ordinary post issue/feedback effects now use

**T03-CAPTURED-EFFECTS is complete**: captured proof/source admission and

**T03-LIBRARY is complete**: admitted human knowledge/decision search and

**T03-WORKER-HTTP is complete**: fixed worker HTTP authentication, current

**T03-WORKER-WIRE is complete**: Factory/System One discovery definitions,

**T03-WORKER-CONTEXT is complete**: admitted worker assignment/lineage reads,

**T03-WORKER-CONSULTATIONS is complete**: bounded admitted System One questions,

**T03-WORKER-RESULTS is complete**: recorded worker result bindings, terminal

**T03-PROOF-CAPTURE is complete**: canonical source/author/revision and current
resource admission, retained-proof reuse and trusted issuance capture now share

**T03-APP is complete** at the selected Linux extraction boundary: all seven
Fountain product route adapters now bind the same shared product router as the
native application, with one canonical account/store and lazy service ports.
The native server now consumes explicit startup recovery; configured connector/
runtime admission remains with its consumer slices.
**T03-CONTRIBUTION-RECOVERY is complete**: new claims hold proved PostgreSQL
producer-session ownership through settlement. Bounded recovery preserves live

model replay or invitation.
**T03-SERVER is complete** for the selected Linux server stage: the actual native
executable opens its owned profile, recovers released assessments before readiness
within the startup budget, and drains/stops cleanly. Live/unowned claims and
unobserved executions stay retained; connected execution remains a later slice.
**T04-RESPONSES is complete**: the eight defining Factory request/run/output/work/

**T04-PROGRESS is complete**: read-only overview, plan and direction/history

**T04-DETAIL is complete**: Work detail/interventions now use shared transport,

**T04-VERIFICATION is complete**: application-verification retry, repair requests

**T04-VERIFICATION-RECOVERY is complete**: retry/repair requests persist under
admitted account/profile and canonical repository scope, recover exact targets
without automatic submission and require fresh issue-zero run scope before replay.
**T04-ALLOWANCE is complete**: verification limits now use one shared control,
typed contracts and scoped pending increases, with exact receipt/current-head

**T04-REPAIR is complete**: repair grants, withdrawals and recorded history now

**T04-ACTIVITY is complete**: recorded activity and display preferences now use

**T04-LIBRARY is complete**: knowledge/decision search, paging and revision history

**T04-FEED-LIFETIME is complete**: feed page/conversation/control requests now share
a cancellable context and captured runtime generation; retired responses cannot

**T04-ARTIFACT-LIFETIME is complete**: card/reply previews receive scoped runtime

**T04-FEED-ACCESS is complete**: current feed/conversation denial clears cached
facts and child previews, stops polling and blocks commands until explicit fresh

**T04-FEED-EXAMPLES is complete**: thirteen production feed stories cover the
required read/submission states through one declared peer, including real revision
CAS. Issued posts now settle across filter changes under captured account/runtime

**T04-FEED-EDIT-LIFETIME is complete**: live revision saves and change-review
handoffs survive filter changes under captured account/runtime scope, validate

**T03-POST-RETRY-RECEIPTS is complete**: exact retry commands and scoped immutable
receipts commit atomically with the existing post/intake transition in the shared
command ledger, including unchanged-revision retries. Real PostgreSQL checks
cover replay, changed reuse, concurrency, rollback and native restart/WAL recovery.
The queue contains 143 dependency-ordered slices.
**T03-POST-RETRY-HTTP is complete**: the shared service/HTTP and current caller
use exact command identity and immutable receipts, with current visibility/author
admission for replay and read-only recovery. Capture belongs only to new commits;
late capture failures cannot mark newer writing as waiting. PostgreSQL/HTTP checks
cover lost replies and handler/store reopen; Fountain proxy and browser cutovers
pass. **T04-FEED-REVISION-RECOVERY is complete**: scoped pending revision commands
persist before dispatch, explicit recovery reads exact receipts without automatic
mutation, and saved retries preserve original intent separately from newer writing.
Browser reload, storage failures, mismatched/replaced records and retired lifetimes
are qualified; the feed's fourteen declared stories include a lost revision reply.
**T04-APP-COMPOSITION is complete**: a production shared frame now selects the
existing Feed, requests, work overview/detail/plan, Knowledge and Watch controls
through typed host-admitted routes/bindings. Browser checks qualify navigation,
drafts, all seven views, rejected/delayed admission, retirement and theme switching.
The 52-source product closure imports no host or stories. T04-UI is next ready
and stays Partial for remaining ownership/recovery joins before native consumers.
**T04-FEED-REVIEW-RECOVERY is complete**: source-bound review handoffs persist
before dispatch and recover recorded draft receipts through explicit reads,
preserving the original revision/intent/predecessor and current actor scope.
Browser reload, storage failure, missing/mismatched facts and retirement are
qualified. Fifteen feed stories include unknown change-review results.
Remaining pending/draft recovery and host assembly stay in T04-UI. Current
scoped pending posts now preserve their command through remount/storage denial
and recover a missing nonce after reload; historical unscoped draft/action
recovery remains an explicit T14-UPGRADE requirement. Run-status view/verification/repair reads now join canonical
repositories through their native Project association. Delivery-repair admission
now receives the admitted canonical owner separately from native command
attribution. Verification-allowance increases also receive explicit authenticated
principal attribution independently of canonical ownership, preserving captured
commands on replay. Spaces now resolves its visible native Project's canonical
repository before Factory authority/control reads and run-view attachment;
conflicting bindings retain the recorded run and mark Factory data incomplete.
Request drafts also use the shared storage fallback, preserving their scoped
recovery record through component remounts when browser storage is denied.
Environment grants now record the canonical owner separately from the native
withdrawal principal and native Project ownership.
Appliance composition now translates the captured execution actor into a native
Fountain user only in the outgoing host launch, before native credential custody.
T02-ENGINE was split into concrete consumer
cutovers before implementation; its final closure/provider qualification remains.

The Linux completion boundary includes every row in the table. D1/D2/D3 gate activation of
their named capabilities; D5 gates any claim of issue-only collaborator parity.
A credential, host capability or authorized real fixture that is unavailable is
a concrete blocker, not permission to mark a simulated journey complete.

**Later platform:** T00-DARWIN follows T02-ENGINE and the completed Linux path.
Qualify the actual Mac dependency closure, native PG, keychain, WKWebView,
executor and packaging there. The known Darwin SDK peer-credential failure does
not block Linux slices or count as fixed by a Linux build. Windows remains out
of scope. Re-resolve upstream inputs for each new implementation/build attempt.

### One-slice execution rule

1. Select the first unfinished row whose prerequisites are complete. Record its
   state as Active in this table and state its concrete finish condition before
   changing code. Do not dispatch concurrent implementation slices or agents.
2. Implement only that slice and its necessary fixes, configuration and docs.
   If a row is too large for one bounded result, split that row into named
   producer/consumer slices here first; keep one active slice and explicit edges.
3. Run its smallest meaningful real integration/native checks under AGENTS.md.
   Preserve passing evidence and unrelated working edits. A fixture-only UI or
   a build cannot stand in for its required connected/installed behavior.
4. Record the actual result and evidence in this backlog. Mark Complete only
   when its finish condition passes. Record a partial or blocked result honestly;
   a slice checkpoint never completes the whole goal.
5. End the implementation turn at that slice boundary. On the next goal turn,
   continue the same incomplete slice or select the next ready row. If blocked,
   record the exact missing producer/input and work on the next independent ready
   row. Do not weaken dependencies, activate unsupported actions or request the
   same permission repeatedly. The goal stays active while useful work remains.

### Why the order changed

- Provider identities and neutral ports precede their service/UI consumers;
  already-working feed extraction is preserved as partial T04 work.
- Desktop lifecycle produces a functioning local shell before connection reads;
  it no longer requires the connected data that T06 must produce later.
- Fountain normalization and admitted operations precede its HTTPS gateway.
  GitHub-connected desktop views can finish independently. Fountain login,
  remote placement and gateway access precede that provider’s desktop activation.
- Human collaboration writes precede editable issue/PR completion and do not
  require an agent executor. Automatic intake and external PR adoption have
  separate provider slices, so a Fountain gate cannot block GitHub automation.
- Placement/generation enforcement precedes native dispatch and unattended
  automation. Native executor retirement joins the supervisor in T09, before
  automatic issue intake is enabled.
- Linux packaging precedes installed acceptance; upgrade and shared-change proof
  consume that installed result. macOS qualification is a later platform task.

`lib/desktop-runtime/src/supervisor.rs` defines `NativeSupervisor`. It claims a
private profile lock before PG/bootstrap, starts the existing owned native
PostgreSQL component, prepares one fresh backend capability and launches the
actual Go executable with its fixed private configuration path. A dedicated
owner thread remains alive for its children even if the public handle moves
between threads. Linux parent-death setup retires the actual children after
abrupt owner death. Direct PG callers must retain their spawning thread; the
existing direct driver stays on its main thread.

supervisor unavailable and retires its remaining child; it does not restart work.

retirement or an unexpected child exit reports failure rather than a clean stop.

execution or recovery authority.

### T05-CREDENTIALS checkpoint — 2026-11-02 (Complete)

The previous goal turn completed native lifecycle and real guest OS wake proof;
it was concrete progress. This turn implemented only the next ready credential
slice. Linux account custody now lives in
`lib/desktop-runtime/src/credentials.rs`, consumed by the production host.

The implementation uses the current Secret Service Rust client directly with
encrypted D-Bus sessions and Rust crypto. The login session's existing OS service
owns the encrypted keyring and unlock behavior; there is no application plaintext
token file or keyring passphrase command. Items are scoped by application,
retained profile ID, provider, HTTPS instance, opaque remote account identity and
connection. Account IDs are not restricted to numeric representations. Stored
metadata means a saved credential, not a verified provider connection or execution
authority. Native T06/T10 login consumers must supply remotely verified identities.

Native-only `Token` and `TokenCapability` have no Serialize/Debug implementation.
Token buffers are zeroized on drop, with an 8 KiB visible-ASCII input limit.
Capabilities bind one native owner, connection and credential revision for 30
seconds. Each use fetches fresh OS state and rejects withdrawn, replaced, expired
or retired authority before lending bytes to a trusted native operation. The
consumer must bound that operation and keep its token out of browser state,
backend configuration and logs. Keyring operations, including access queued behind
another operation, have a five-second deadline; metadata result counts are bounded.

Reauthentication preserves a current connection ID, replaces the token and
rotates its revision. Withdrawal first records/syncs an empty `0600` denial
marker in the profile's `0700` `withdrawn-credentials/` directory, then attempts
OS deletion. Locked/unavailable deletion is reported as failure while denial
remains effective across reopening; explicit successful native reauthentication
can clear it. Failure to persist the marker is not represented as completed
withdrawal. Duplicate/corrupt metadata and unavailable/locked services fail
visibly without forwarding raw D-Bus error text or secret material.

The production Tauri bridge adds only `credential_status` and
`credential_withdraw`. The webview cannot supply a keyring service/profile,
read a token, write a token or request an arbitrary secret. Withdrawal retires
the browser generation and observations. Runtime replacement/loss and Quit retire
the native credential owner; closing a window retains it. No account is bound
to the Go backend by storage alone. Provider login, refresh, live private reads
and provider-specific remote revocation are T06-GITHUB/T10-GATEWAY consumers.

Actual integration evidence used a **real GNOME Keyring daemon** on a private
D-Bus session, with a generated nonempty unlock password supplied only on stdin,
private HOME/XDG data/runtime directories, generated fixture token bytes and
the actual Cage/Wayland/WebKit production application. The personal session and
keyring were not used or modified. The existing `native-check` feature was
extended with `--check-credentials`; no new unit tests, test roots or allowlist
exceptions were introduced.

The final check proved:

- Store/read through the real encrypted service; native owner/profile isolation;
  opaque account IDs; same-connection reauthentication and refusal of the old
  token capability after rotation.
- Actual webview metadata has only account/connection/origin/provider/state;
  attempts to invoke token retrieval or token storage are rejected. Withdrawal
  from the webview removes the OS item and advances the browser generation;
  existing capabilities and a reopened owner refuse the withdrawn connection.
- The external driver locks the real default collection. Status reports locked,
  capability creation/use refuse, and withdrawal reports locked while its durable
  marker denies use after reopening the owner.
- The driver stops the actual daemon; status reports unavailable rather than
  an empty/connected account list. Persistent withdrawal denial still applies.
  Restarting/unlocking that same daemon retains a separate untouched token,
  which is read freshly and compared with its original generated bytes.
- The real on-disk login keyring contains none of the fixture plaintext tokens.
  The observer waits through the actual 30-second lease and confirms expiry,
  then mints a fresh capability and confirms explicit owner retirement. Remaining
  fixture items are deleted; ordered product Quit exits 0. Fixture services and
  native children are terminal; the personal keyring remains untouched.

Authoritative final logs are
`/home/vince/factory-credential-check-20261102-3/native.log` and
`/home/vince/factory-credential-native-driver-3.log`. The live driver reports
real lock, stop, restart/unlock and native exit 0. Its retained program is

read exactly one bounded chronological provider page (1–50) or one positive

internal/github/check_runs.go implements PullCheckRuns with the existing SDK.
It resolves the selected stable repository, captures the actual PR ID/full head,
reads one bounded page of 1–50 check runs for that SHA, rechecks the same PR/head,
then rechecks repository identity/visibility before returning. Discovery accepts
empty head only on page one; later pages require the full captured head. A wrong
requested or changed observed head returns ErrChecksChanged. Each check run must
have an actual positive ID, name, captured head and selected repository check-run
URL, with no duplicate IDs. The whole operation shares the existing eight-second
budget, GET/origin restriction and response cap.

Provider-local records preserve actual check-run IDs (not Actions job/run IDs),
names, nullable raw status/conclusion, original timestamps/details URL and
nullable app/output title/summary/text/annotation-count facts. Known state and
conclusion values normalize explicitly; absent/future values stay unknown. URLs
and rich text are untrusted display data, never fetched or interpreted as action
authority. Annotation bodies are not fetched. No required flag, aggregate CI
success, Actions job identity or merge/execution capability is invented.

The SDK query explicitly uses filter=all to retain available older attempts.
The response total is documented as the provider window. Official GitHub docs
state that this endpoint is limited to check runs from the 1000 most recent
check suites when a ref has more; it does not establish an all-time complete
catalogue. The combined canonical gate still must account for provider retention,
separate statuses, requirements and app/context selection before any action is
enabled. Same-head jobs may also change while paging; these are live pages, not
an atomic checks snapshot. Empty data cannot become proof that no checks apply.

The existing private Go/Rust read boundary adds typed pull_check_runs. Go shares
the producer's page/head validation and forbids unrelated base/review/state
selectors. Rust validates query bounds, repository/PR selectors and full-head
continuations, then checks successful response account/connection/repository,
PR kind/number, full observed/requested head, cardinality and every item's SHA.
Head changes map to 409/github_checks_changed. Existing per-call /user matching,
native OS credential postchecks, peer/key/instance, cancellation and IPC response
bounds remain required; no browser token access or authentication fallback exists.

  Failed persistence prevents dispatch. Reopening only checks that original
  command, while retry/cancel are explicit and retain identity, conditions and
  field presence. A durable cancellation cannot turn into submit. Missing,
  unknown, malformed or unfinished outcomes keep pending writing. Capability
  failure disables submit but leaves scoped lookup/cancel available. Successful
  receipts clear only the matching original revision; newer writing survives.
  No-effect/cancel keeps both differing versions until the user explicitly
  discards the original edit. Failed writes preserve their persisted baseline;
  explicit reload merges only matching pending intent, and unknown bytes stay
  blocked and untouched. Closing the editor retains its draft.

## T06-GITHUB-DEVICE — private device authorization (2026-11-03, Complete)

The owner supplied Factory’s public OAuth client ID. Split the native authorization producer from the full connected-provider consumer before implementation; only this row was Active. Implementation commit `8191de9` uses the existing private peer/key/instance/coordinator admission and upstream OAuth polling implementation. The two exact native endpoints are not browser routes. The shared engine remains independent of GitHub and its OAuth SDK.

Go owns fixed-origin networking and bounded responses; Rust owns an opaque, captured-instance authorization with a serializable user-code/verification-URL prompt only. ## T09-NATIVE-PROCESS — verified headless process authority (2026-11-04)

Completed the N3 process producer in lib/desktop-runtime/src/execution. Rust
captures bounded native ELF bytes into a sealed memfd with SHA-256 identity;
source replacement cannot change the admitted executable. A native-only typed
invocation supplies a private directory, explicit argv/environment, PTY size and
finite resource limits. There is no serialized shell/process API, inherited
parent environment, Tauri dependency, Go product policy or SQL owner here.

A private exclusive native lock and its file identity bind the kernel namespace
to its configured profile/storage owner. Another directory with the same profile
label cannot adopt live work. Admission requires an actual user-delegated
cgroup-v2 subtree with CPU/memory/process controllers and permission to migrate
the child. Limits are installed and the child enters its scope before executable
code can fork. PTY descriptors acquire CLOEXEC atomically across concurrent forks.
The monitor owns boot/start identity, direct-child exit, hard time/output bounds,
cancellation and detached-descendant retirement independently of Go polling.
Slow output-file writes start after the child/tree control pass. Output remains
private and bounded, and truncation stays explicitly incomplete.

Dropping an observation handle does not cancel admitted native work. Owner
retirement stops admission, cancels kernel scopes and joins all monitors. Direct
exit, resource retirement, complete output and credential retirement remain
separate facts. Unconfirmed resource cleanup fences further admission and stays
uncertain through retirement; exclusive reopen retires the retained owned scope
without inventing an old exit code. Empty profile scopes retire with their owner.
This is trusted same-user execution, not hostile-process isolation or a promise
to force an uninterruptible kernel task to disappear.

This migration found and fixed OAuth status handling in
`github_provider/transport.rs`: a grant body can only succeed on HTTP 200;
HTTP 400–499 must carry a bounded JSON OAuth error, and redirects refuse even
when their body resembles a full grant. Unknown outcomes remain unconfirmed.
The prior Go SDK's incidental form-response acceptance is retired: the current
Rust client requests JSON explicitly, and unexpected form bodies are qualified
as refusal. Rust's existing bounded-body outcome is 413, rather than the old
Go observer's generic 502. These are explicit contract distinctions.

### T11-WRITES — durable one-shot comment dispatch producer (2026-11-05)

`factory_commands` row; it does not create a second operation journal or an
authenticated Go provider connector. `pkg/factory/command_dispatch.go`,
`pkg/store/factory_human_comment_dispatch.go`, `pkg/store/schema_command_dispatch.go`
and `pkg/store/schema.go` define the local dispatch reservation and schema 81.

An exact captured human comment with a persisted, validated `not_observed`
lookup can acquire one reservation under the existing row lock. Only the caller
receiving a successful commit may dispatch once. Reading `reserved` cannot
recover ownership. Unknown replies, later absence observations, process restart
and WAL recovery cannot release the reservation. Finished commands cannot
acquire it. This is local dispatch eligibility, never current provider permission,
remote absence, a cancellation guarantee or evidence that a request was sent.

The actual schema-80 upgrade marks every existing command `legacy_unknown`,
retaining its captured bytes/outcomes and refusing new dispatch through this
protocol. It does not invent a historical attempt time. Fresh rows default to
`unclaimed`. Fresh and upgraded databases use the same identity, terminal-outcome
and irreversible-dispatch trigger. Existing remote-journal adapters retain their
own protocol; this producer does not alter Fountain's dispatch behavior.

### T11-WRITES — Rust comment effect producer (2026-11-05)

The complete native provider owner now defines one bounded issue/PR ordinary
comment creation operation in `github_provider/comments.rs`, using the existing
transport owner and the shared repository/subject/record decoders. There is no
authenticated Go HTTP implementation or browser-facing arbitrary request port.
`Comment` pins the remote repository, immutable subject identity, kind, number
and exact human writing; the expected native account is separate. Go canonical
identity and durable command/outcome policy remain Go responsibilities.

The operation validates its 64 KiB UTF-8 writing contract and selectors before
network use, verifies `/user`, resolves the selected repository and subject, and
refuses changed identity/subject, a locked or unknown-lock discussion, or an
archived/disabled/unknown-read-only repository. These are bounded preflight
observations, not atomic provider revision guards. Repository push permission is
not used as comment authority. GitHub still enforces the actual comment request;
no positive comment-permission admission proof is inferred from these reads.

Comment operations serialize across clones of the same provider owner, with at
least one second between POST starts. The existing fixed HTTPS host, no redirect,
no retry, bounded header/body handling and joined owner are retained. The fixed
comment POST has a 1 MiB response bound; the whole operation, including queue/
pacing/preflight waits, has an eight-second deadline and observes owner retirement.
Only 201 plus a successfully decoded response with the exact parent URL,
comment URL/ID, author and unchanged body yields `Created`. Failure after the
dispatch boundary—including provider refusal, timeout, lost reply, malformed or
misbound success—is conservatively `Indeterminate`. A failure before that
boundary is `NotSent`. Neither outcome authorizes an automatic retry. A dropped
caller may receive no outcome; its durable reservation must remain fenced.

`lib/desktop-runtime/src/github_provider/thread_resolution.rs` supplies one fixed
resolve or unresolve effect through the existing native transport. The public
semantic request binds immutable numeric repository/PR identity, PR number,

Current [GitHub schema](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/pulls#resolvereviewthreadinput)
was checked on 2026-11-05. The two mutations accept a thread ID and return the
thread, without an expected conversation revision or repository condition. Only
`threadId` is sent; no Copilot resolution reason, automatic agent request or
remote-deduplication claim is added. The returned resolver is checked against the
authenticated account for resolve; unresolve requires an explicitly null resolver
and does not invent a mutation actor field that the payload lacks.

The effect shares the existing mutation mutex/pacing across Client clones and
clips its entire lifetime, including waits/preflight, to eight seconds. It checks
current account, repository readonly flags, PR identity/lock and the defining

An already matching state is a distinct known no-send result with no receipt;
it can never attribute an earlier uncertain effect. A non-null supplied original
